chunks: From him, from Ahmad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Amr ibn Uthman al-Juhani, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, Allah does not change His decision due to ignorance.

key_terms.يَبْدُ: it becomes manifest / changes (jussive of bada'—the theological term for God's alteration of a previously decreed matter)

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq (AS) say about whether Allah's bada' arises from ignorance, according to al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) here provides a theological clarification of the Shia doctrine of al-bada' — the notion that God can alter or manifest a change in His decreed affairs. This hadith establishes a crucial boundary: unlike a human being who changes his mind upon learning something new, Allah's bada' is never the result of prior ignorance. God's alteration of decree flows from His perfect and unchanging knowledge, affirming divine omniscience alongside the reality of bada'.
